en: The Method for Contemplating the Mind through Eating, by the Tiantai Master Zhizhe:

Once the seat has been prepared, one waits for the *vinaya-dhara* (ritual master) to signal the commencement. After the bell has been struck, one joins the palms in reverence and makes offerings to the Three Jewels as a single entity.
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, he performs the Buddha-work. Next, he produces food and bestows it upon the six realms of existence;

this immediately symbolizes the six *pāramitās*. Only then does he accept this food. Now, food is the external life-force of sentient beings. If one does not enter into contemplation (*vipaśyanā*), it merely nourishes birth and death (*saṃsāra*).
If one can know how to enter contemplation, one distinguishes whether birth and death have limits or are limitless, regardless of whether one is begging for alms.
When partaking of pure food with the assembly of the pure, one must perform contemplation. As for this contemplation:

one should fear that the old food within this body has all been nourished by ignorance and afflictions, thereby producing birth and death; whereas the food currently being consumed is entirely Prajñā.
One should imagine the old food exiting sequentially through the pores. Once the food has exited, the path of the mind is immediately opened. Then, one consumes the new food.

It illuminates all darkness and brings about the perfection of *prajñā*. Therefore, the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra* states: "That which is equal regarding food is also equal regarding the Dharma. This serves as clear evidence.
By means of this food, one accomplishes the food of *prajñā*, which is able to nourish the *dharmakāya*. Once the *dharmakāya* is established, liberation is attained.
This is the illumination of these three virtues (*triguṇa*) by means of this food. It is neither new nor old; yet there is the "ancient food."
For this reason, there is the "newness" of new food; this is called the provisional (prajñapti). When one seeks the old, it is not found; when one seeks the new, it is not found.

Ultimate emptiness and stillness is called the contemplation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vipaśyanā). As for the eater, how could they eat anything as "new"? Since there is no new food, how can food be obtained?
Yet the eater does not depart from the old food that sustains the body, while the new food provides further benefit. Because of this—
The harmony of conditions cannot be distinguished as preceding or succeeding; this is termed the "Middle. That which is the Middle is itself the provisional and the empty;

that which is the empty is itself the Middle and the provisional; that which is the provisional is itself the empty and the Middle. This inconceivable state is called the Middle Way. Furthermore, the Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra says:

It is neither the presence of afflictions nor the absence of afflictions; it is neither entering a state of meditative concentration nor arising from a state of meditative concentration. This is called the Dharma of nutriment.
